evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.34: animōs adflīgere et dēbilitāre metū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally to dash to the ground; of the spirits, to cast down. Afflīctus is downcast, wretched (Lewis & Short).
To let one’s spirits sink: what a person does who is depressed. Its opposite is animōs tollere (Lucilius, in Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: sī vīcerint, efferunt sē laetitiā; victī dēbilitantur animōsque dēmittunt
phrases.english: if they win, they are carried away with joy; beaten, they lose their strength and their spirits sink (of children at play)

sources: Lewis & Short: affligo · Lewis & Short: demitto
